    Substitute $Q(x) = Ax + B$ into the left-hand side (LHS):
    $$\text{LHS} = (Aa_3 + B) - ((Aa_1 + B) + (Aa_2 + B))$$
    $$\text{LHS} = Aa_3 + B - Aa_1 - B - Aa_2 - B$$

    The right-hand side (RHS) remains:
    $$\text{RHS} = a_3^2 - a_1^2 - a_2^2$$

    $$A(a_3 - a_1 - a_2) - B = a_3^2 - a_1^2 - a_2^2$$

    $$A(a_3 - a_1 - a_2) + (-1)B - (a_3^2 - a_1^2 - a_2^2) = 0$$

        $$-1 = 0$$

    The requirement that the identity holds for an arbitrary polynomial $Q(x)$ of degree less than 2 leads to the contradiction $-1=0$ when examining the coefficient of $B$. Therefore, no such set of distinct positive integers $\{a_1, a_2, a_3\}$ exists that satisfies the required identity for all allowed polynomials $Q(x)$.
